answer: Each epoch, a random jury of bonded agents audits every new identity before it can vote. A jury seat requires a basalt-hard stake locked for the whole season, and a juror who rubber-stamps a fake loses it. An attacker facing an ocean of honest stakers cannot know which ember of the jury will inspect their sock-puppets, so capturing a majority means bribing most of the bonded set — a cost that scales with the network, not with the number of fakes they mint.
